scenes.heading: Powerful vocabulary and sentences
scenes.sub: Same idea, more power: choose words and shape sentences
scenes.say: Two students can have the same idea, but one sounds flat and the other sounds alive. The difference is word choice and sentence shape. Let's make your writing sound alive.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: A builder picks the exact tool, not ten random ones
scenes.science: A writer picks the exact word, not a pile of vague ones
scenes.breaks: a tool is right or wrong; words also carry feelings, so the right word must match the mood too.
scenes.say: Think of a builder. They don't bring ten random tools; they pick the exact one for the job. Writing is the same. One precise word beats a pile of vague ones.

scenes.heading: Vague versus precise
scenes.say: Compare. Walked slowly becomes trudged. Very big dog becomes a Great Dane. A nice pie becomes a flaky pie. Precise nouns and verbs carry the meaning in fewer words. And watch the feeling: notorious means famous for something bad.

scenes.heading: Three sentence types
points: Compound: The ferry left, and gulls followed.
Complex: Although seas were rough, it left.
scenes.say: Mix three sentence types. A simple sentence has one clause: the ferry left. A compound sentence joins two with and, but or so. A complex sentence adds a part that can't stand alone, starting with a word like although, when or because.

scenes.heading: Combine the choppy sentences
scenes.question: The bell rang. Students rushed out. They were noisy. They left their bags behind.
lines: When the bell rang, students rushed noisily out…
scenes.say: Let's combine four choppy sentences. Turn the time into when the bell rang. Keep the main action, students rushed out. Turn noisy into noisily. And turn the last idea into leaving their bags behind. One smooth, strong sentence.

Quick recap. Strong verbs beat very and extra adverbs. Match the word's feeling to the sentence. Mix simple, compound and complex sentences. Vary your openers, and use one fresh comparison at a time. Now try the practice questions!
